learning: Iteration 8 showed the drivetrain lever works on the s-bend (0.1496 to 0.1604) with slalom oscillation at 0.157. The race will show whether that gain continues at 0.09 m or whether the controller must absorb more turn gain. The kp change is confounded with the track change, so if oscillation rises the Integrator should report it separately.
notes: Adopts the Builder's wheel_track 0.09 m test with the sensing held at the iteration 8 layout. kp is lowered to 4.6 to offset the roughly 11 percent higher turn gain from the narrower track, so the slalom oscillation stays below the 0.16 trigger.
rationale: Iteration 8 (wheel_track 0.10 m, y 0.08 m, kp 5.0) raised s-bend progress to 0.1604 and the oval to 0.167, with slalom steering_oscillation at 0.157, close to the 0.16 trigger. Forward lead has plateaued (iterations 6 and 7), so the drivetrain is the remaining lever. The Builder's proposal narrows wheel_track to 0.09 m at mass 0.8 kg, sensors unchanged at 16 mm, x = ±0.048 m, y = 0.08 m. Narrowing the track raises effective turn gain by roughly 11 percent, which would push slalom oscillation toward or past 0.16. To keep the steering gain near the iteration 8 level I scale kp by 1/1.11, giving kp 4.6 (from 5.0). Iteration 3 showed kp alone does not move the s-bend, so this is a stability adjustment, not a progress lever. ki 0.05, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.5 and last_direction line loss are unchanged. Weights stay proportional to x so a positive signal steers left. Expected: s-bend progress about 0.16 to 0.165, slalom oscillation below 0.16. These are predictions only.
